cards.q: What is IMAP and how does it handle mail?
cards.a: IMAP (TCP 143) keeps mail on the server and synchronizes it across clients, keeping folders, read-state, and messages consistent; it also supports server-side search and partial fetch, and its secure variant is IMAPS on TCP 993.

Mail lives on the server (port 143, secure 993), synchronizes across clients, is an online protocol, and uses server-side folders; clients keep talking to the server so nothing lives only on one device.

cards.q: How do IMAP and POP3 compare?
cards.a: IMAP keeps mail on the server and syncs across multiple clients with server folders and search, using ports 143/993; POP3 downloads and usually deletes mail, lacks multi-device sync, uses a single INBOX, and uses ports 110/995.

cards.q: What are the basic IMAP operations?
cards.a: LOGIN authenticates, SELECT INBOX opens a folder, FETCH n BODY[] retrieves a message, SEARCH UNSEEN runs a server-side query, STORE +FLAGS (Seen) marks mail read, and CLOSE/LOGOUT finishes; commands are prefix-tagged, e.g. a01 SELECT INBOX.

cards.q: What are the IMAP security ports?
cards.a: 143 is plaintext and 993 is IMAPS over TLS; use 993 or STARTTLS because mail on 143 is sniffable.

cards.q: When should you choose IMAP versus POP3?
cards.a: Choose IMAP when using phone plus laptop plus webmail, for server backup because mail is retained, and where multi-device sync matters; choose POP3 for offline single-device use and minimal server load.

cards.q: Why is IMAP better than POP3 for DLP and backup?
cards.a: IMAP keeps mail on the mail servers, so central backup and DLP work better than with POP3 where data lands only on endpoints.

cards.q: What should network operations watch for with IMAP?
cards.a: Allow TCP 143/993 and monitor for bulk login attempts, and check credentials on bad-login reports, folder config on missing folders, and client settings when sync drift appears.

cards.q: The exam's memorizable IMAP versus POP3 contrast is what?
cards.a: IMAP = synchronized online; POP3 = download offline.

cards.q: How would you troubleshoot an IMAP connection reset?
cards.a: It is often a TLS-versus-plaintext mismatch: connect with 993 when encryption is required rather than 143, and verify the ACL and credentials.
